# knowledge management

> Proof of concept for the SD Worx challenge "Unlock the Knowledge Within: Find it. Understand it. Trust it." at the Tectonic Hackathon (30 September 2026). It is a single-page, offline knowledge manager that combines scattered HR documents into one summary per company and country, using a fixed template. When documents disagree, the summary uses the most recent approved information. For every section of a summary, the app shows all the documents that were considered, so a reader can check that the right one was used.

## Challenge it addresses

SD Worx asked: "How might we turn fragmented organisational knowledge into a trusted shared resource?" The challenge describes the moment of doubt when several documents answer the same question and one is outdated, one has no owner and one applies to another country. This project targets that moment for employee working conditions. It gives one answer per company and country, and makes visible where each part of the answer comes from and what was set aside.

## How it works

- Structure: Company -> Country -> summary "Employee Working Conditions" -> one folder per template section -> the source documents about that section.
- Summary template (taken from a sample policy summary):
  - a title and the line "Current approved policy — Effective <date>"
  - seven sections: Working hours, Overtime, Vacation, Remote work, Sick leave, Meal vouchers, and Parental and special leave; each has a bold value and short detail lines
  - a footer with the policy owner, status, effective date and version
- In SUMMARY.txt, each section ends with a "Source:" line naming the document or documents it was taken from.
- Resolution rule: when sources disagree, the most recent approved policy or announcement wins. Superseded documents and draft proposals are never used. The detail line records what changed and what the older source said.
- The app sorts documents into section folders by keyword. A full policy covers every section, so it appears in all seven folders. Documents that match no section go into "Other documents".
- Clicking a section in the summary lists every document considered for it:
  - the document(s) used first, then the rest, newest first
  - each document's date, status and owner
  - the sentences where that document mentions the section
  - the reason a document was not used: older, superseded, draft, or "newer than the one used", which is a warning
- Trust signals per document: owner or sender, status (approved / unverified / superseded / draft), date, review date, duplicate text, and numeric conflicts with other documents.
- Conflict detection is a heuristic that runs in the browser.
  - It compares numbers only between documents of the same company and country, and only when both numbers are about the same template section and have the same kind of unit (money, %, days, weeks or hours, and the same period).
  - Each number is compared with its best-matching counterpart in the other document.
  - Dates, times, e-mail addresses and links are ignored.
- A summary is flagged when, for a section:
  - a newer document that is neither a draft nor superseded was not used, or
  - a named source is missing, or
  - a source was added or edited in the app after the summary was compiled.
- Trustworthiness score: every opened document shows "Trust 6/10". This is a deliberate placeholder. The function trustScore() in index.html returns 6 for every document, and no scoring algorithm exists yet.

## How to run

Open index.html in a browser (Chrome or Edge recommended). There is no build step, no server and no network access. Data is kept in the browser's localStorage. "Reset demo data" in the sidebar restores the built-in example documents.

## Files

- [index.html](index.html): the whole application (HTML, CSS and JavaScript in one file), plus the built-in example documents in a JSON block with id "seed-data".
- [README.md](README.md): project description, how to run, and what is unfinished.
- Company A/<Country>/Employee Working Conditions/ and Company B/<Country>/Employee Working Conditions/: SUMMARY.txt plus the source documents as plain .txt files. These are the same texts as the built-in data, and "Import folder" in the app reads this layout.
- [robots.txt](robots.txt): allows all crawlers.

## Example data (all fictional)

The example data covers Company A and Company B, each with America, Belgium and France: 6 summaries and 39 source documents. General legal references reflect the rules as generally known:
- Belgium: a 38-hour average working week, 20 legal vacation days, and 20 days of birth leave for the co-parent.
- France: the 35-hour week, overtime at +25% for the first 8 hours and +50% beyond, and 25 days of paternity leave.
- United States: overtime at 1.5 times the regular rate above 40 hours (FLSA), and FMLA job protection.

Company-specific numbers are invented.

Conflicts planted on purpose, and how each summary resolves them (the most recent source wins):
- Company A / Belgium:
  - Remote work: the policy (v3.1, effective 1 January 2026) says 2 days; an email of 2 March 2026 says 1 day from April. The summary uses 1 day.
  - The superseded policy v2.4 differs on vacation (20 vs 21 days, maximum 25 vs 26), remote work (3 days) and meal vouchers (€7). It is not used.
- Company A / France:
  - RTT days: the policy says 10; an email of 5 January 2026 says 11. The summary uses 11.
  - Titres-restaurant: the policy says €9; an email of 2 February 2026 says €10 from March. The summary uses €10.
  - The superseded policy v1.3 (39 hours, 20 RTT days) is not used.
- Company A / America:
  - Remote work: the handbook says 2 days; an email of 10 September 2026 says 1 day from October. The summary uses 1 day.
  - Sick days: the handbook says 5; an email of 1 April 2026 says 7. The summary uses 7.
  - A 2022 email and the superseded handbook v3.2 give 12 PTO days. They are not used.
  - "payrollemail.txt" (an undated, unsigned email about a $75,000 minimum wage) matches no template section. It appears under "Other documents".
- Company B / Belgium:
  - Meal vouchers: the policy says €7; an email of 1 June 2026 says €8 from July. The summary uses €8.
  - Sick leave: the policy requires a certificate from the first day; an email of 15 January 2026 removes that for the first day, up to 3 times a year. The summary uses the email.
  - A four-day-week draft is newer but is a draft. It is not used.
- Company B / France:
  - Remote work: the policy says 3 days; an email of 20 April 2026 says 2 days from May. The summary uses 2 days.
  - Employer share of titres-restaurant: the policy says 50%; an email of 8 January 2026 says 60%. The summary uses 60%.
  - A superseded 2019 document says 39 hours. It is not used.
- Company B / America:
  - Remote work: the handbook says 2 days; an email of 10 September 2026 says 1 day from October. The summary uses 1 day.
  - Parental leave: the handbook gives 8 weeks to non-birthing parents; an email of 1 July 2026 gives 16 weeks to all parents. The summary uses 16 weeks.
  - A draft PTO update (15 days) is newer but is a draft. It is not used.

## Security

- A Content-Security-Policy blocks all network requests, external scripts, form submissions and base-URL changes.
- User content is inserted into the page only as text, never as HTML.
- Imports accept .txt files up to 2 MB only.
- There are no accounts, API keys or secrets.

## Limitations

- The trust score is a fixed placeholder (6/10).
- The summaries were written in advance using the resolution rule above. They are not generated when the app runs. The app checks them but does not rewrite them.
- Only .txt sources are supported.
- The app runs in a single browser for a single user. There is no shared backend, so there is no authentication or authorisation.
- Documents are sorted into sections by keyword, and conflicts are only detected when they are stated as numbers.
